author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can view every specialty with the veterinarians who hold it
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster, and shows all specialties on one page without paging.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name with first name before last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page — the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
All specialties render on a single page with no paging control.
A specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by no one.
Specialties are presented in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians within each specialty.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
notes: Product owner fixed the route as GET /specialties.html (behavioral surface; kept out of PRD prose per the PRD's no-URL convention). Read-only view of the existing vet/specialty data; the inverse of the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001). Full name is first name then last name. New REQ-VET-003 in the vet/specialty directory family (VET-002 is superseded, so numbering skips it).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is another instance of the established feature-package server-rendered-list pattern, entirely within the vet/ package: a @Controller mapping GET /specialties.html (mirror of VetController.showVetList), a declarative Spring Data repository (mirror of VetRepository/PetTypeRepository), and a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets/ using the shared layout fragment. No new module, pattern, integration, or dependency. Governed by the feature-package-organization and server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf ADRs. No durable-memory change: the new contracts (SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository) land in system-design.md via post-implementation doc-sync, not ahead of the code.
integration_points: Reuse the existing VetRepository.findAll() (already @Cacheable("vets")) as the source of veterinarians rather than adding a parallel vet fetch — this is the established mapping the vet directory already renders.
New SpecialtyRepository supplies the complete specialty set; the controller inverts the Vet->Specialty ManyToMany in memory to build each specialty's veterinarian list.
Template reuses fragments/layout.html; the active menu key stays 'vets' (this slice adds no nav item — PRD does not request one).

patterns.description: @Controller + @GetMapping returning a view name with model attributes — copy this shape for /specialties.html, but omit all pagination (findPaginated/addPaginationModel) since the PRD forbids paging: a single findAll, one model attribute, one view name.

Declarative Spring Data lookup repository returning rows in name order — mirror for SpecialtyRepository.findAll() (name-ordered). Do NOT add @Cacheable: follow PetTypeRepository, not VetRepository, to avoid extending the unconfigured-eviction cache noted in system-design Open Question 5.

Vet.getSpecialties() sorts by name via Comparator.comparing(NamedEntity::getName) — mirror this for the stable within-specialty veterinarian order, e.g. Comparator.comparing(Vet::getLastName).thenComparing(Vet::getFirstName).

Full-name rendering ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} and the th:if none-fallback pattern (line 21) — reuse both; render 'none'/held-by-no-one via the existing #{none} message key when a specialty's veterinarian list is empty.

risks.risk: Deriving the specialty set from the veterinarians alone would drop specialties held by no one, violating the acceptance criterion that an unheld specialty still appears.
risks.mitigation: Enumerate specialties from SpecialtyRepository.findAll() (the authoritative complete set); use the vets only to populate each specialty's holder list. The seed data holds all three specialties, so a test must construct an unheld specialty explicitly (WebMvcTest with @MockitoBean on both repositories, following VetControllerTests).

risks.risk: The Vet->Specialty ManyToMany is unidirectional (no back-reference on Specialty), so there is no navigation or single query from a Specialty to its Vets.
risks.mitigation: Invert in the controller: for each specialty, select the vets whose getSpecialties() contains it. Keep this aggregation as a small immutable presentation value (an ordered List of a package-private record such as SpecialtyListing(Specialty, List<Vet>)) so the view model is testable and the ordering is explicit — do not add a bidirectional mapping or mutate the domain entities.

notes: Verdict basis (no IDE oracle connected; grep/read is the weaker basis): confirmed via Read that no SpecialtyController or SpecialtyRepository exists — Specialty (vet/Specialty.java) is a bare NamedEntity with no repository today, and the survey Contracts table lists none. Route GET /specialties.html is the product-owner-fixed contract from the prd-entry notes. This is read-only (GET, no request params, no form binding): it introduces no trust boundary; Thymeleaf default escaping covers XSS on specialty and veterinarian names; it fails closed (empty repositories render an empty page). No autofix records to audit in the log.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The ordering assertion `assertThat(content.indexOf("Linda Douglas")).isLessThan(content.indexOf("Rafael Ortega"))` has a false-pass window. When "Linda Douglas" is absent from the rendered output, `indexOf` returns -1, which is numerically less than any present vet's positive index. The test would pass green even if the controller omitted the alphabetically-first veterinarian entirely, masking the exact defect the ordering criterion exists to catch. A prior existence assertion for both names must precede the relative-position check.

The factory methods `specialty(int id, String name)` and `vet(int id, String firstName, String lastName, Specialty... held)` expose an `id` parameter that is irrelevant to every test outcome. All five test methods pass bare integer literals (1, 2, 3) as IDs, creating Tier-3 mystery values that the brief's three-tier data-naming convention requires to be eliminated. Remove the `id` parameter from both factory signatures and auto-assign IDs internally (e.g., via a private `AtomicInteger` counter), so call sites become `specialty("radiology")` and `vet("Helen", "Leary", radiology)`.
findings.fix: Remove the `id` parameter from both factory method signatures; use a static `AtomicInteger` counter inside each factory to assign a unique ID. Update all five test methods to drop the leading integer argument.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The private `holds` predicate matches a specialty by `getName().equals()` rather than by ID. `BaseEntity` does not override `equals()`/`hashCode()`, so a call to `contains()` would use reference equality and silently fail when the specialty instances from `SpecialtyRepository.findAll()` and from `Vet.getSpecialties()` are different JPA proxy instances. Name comparison is therefore a deliberate workaround — but nothing in the code says so. A reader who does not know `BaseEntity` lacks `equals()` will either wonder why `contains()` was not used, or — worse — 'fix' it to `contains()` and introduce a subtle mismatch bug. The method body is a natural place for a one-line comment: // BaseEntity has no equals()/hashCode(); compare by ID, not reference.
findings.fix: Either add an explanatory comment — // BaseEntity has no equals()/hashCode(); compare by ID, not reference — and switch to `held.getId().equals(specialty.getId())` which makes the identity semantics explicit, or keep name comparison and document that the business rule treats name as the natural key. Either is correct; the silence is not.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 2 requires both 'Specialties are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one' AND 'so are the veterinarians within each specialty'. The test named theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderSpecialtiesStably covers only the second part (vet ordering within a specialty: Douglas before Ortega). The specialty-ordering half — that the controller passes the repository-returned list through to the view without reordering — has no assertion. A future change that accidentally re-sorted or reversed the specialty list would go undetected. Class sweep across all test files confirms no other test provides this coverage.
findings.fix: Extend theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderSpecialtiesStably (or add a companion test) to stub the repository with specialties in a known order and assert they appear in that order on the rendered page, e.g. stub returns [surgery, dentistry] and assertThat(content.indexOf("dentistry")).isLessThan(content.indexOf("surgery")), guarded by a prior .contains("dentistry").contains("surgery") existence assertion using the same pattern applied at line 148.
